A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 72-page study, including Appendices A-P. Full-document text and visual comparisons support reliable matching. The overlapping text on v1 page 67 is recoverable and corresponds to the separated text in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix N report original GNN experiments measuring convergence, test accuracy, and throughput on four graph datasets, including repeated-run results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and results in Section 5 and Appendix N, including the benchmark comparisons and repeated-run tables.

M1.justification: The GNN formulations, full-graph and mini-batch training procedures, uniform neighbor sampling, and CE/MSE objectives are unchanged. No algorithm or model component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate node classification on Reddit, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products, and ogbn-papers100M. Other tasks discussed in Appendix P remain proposed extensions rather than added evaluations.

E2.justification: The same full-graph versus mini-batch comparisons are reported for GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix N retain the same dataset splits, model configurations, hyperparameter sweeps, convergence thresholds, metrics, and training budgets.

E4.justification: The hardware comparisons, batch-size and fan-out sensitivity studies, learning-rate sweeps, and supplementary convergence and generalization analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix N.1 already reports at least three runs with different seeds and the same variance information in v1. Appendix N.7 and Tables 5-12 containing additional runs are present in both; improved placement does not introduce new statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings match throughout, including the appendix plots and Tables 5-12. For example, Table 1 reports the same ogbn-products accuracies of 77.92 for full-graph and 78.80 for mini-batch training in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorems 1-3, the Wasserstein-distance definition, formal assumptions, and appendix proofs and derivations are unchanged. The reflowed extension discussion also retains its mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning Wasserstein-based generalization analysis, different effects of batch and fan-out sizes, and the absence of consistent full-graph superiority.

C2.justification: The interpretations of convergence and generalization, explanations of performance degradation, and applicability discussions in Appendix P are unchanged. Qualifications concerning Tanh and heterogeneous graphs are retained.

D1.justification: The implementation link and Appendix N's hardware, software, sampling, hyperparameter, and training disclosures remain the same. Separating the previously overlapping N.7 text adds no technical information.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning in Section 6 and Appendix O are unchanged. Appendix O's opening moves from page 67 to page 68 without adding or removing cited work or arguments.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 30 January 2026 to v2 dated 5 May 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, and section hierarchy otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 corrects the collision involving Figure 16's caption, Appendix N.7, and Appendix O on v1 page 67. Appendix O starts on page 68, with subsequent text reflowing through page 71 and small alignment adjustments. Figure and table contents are preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 fixes a concrete readability defect: Appendix N.7 overprints the opening related-work text near Figure 16 in v1. Separating these elements and reflowing Appendices O-P makes the material readable. The benefit is limited to presentation; the scientific arguments, experiments, results, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
